window: reset release to end of the one-case command (whole kernel launch sequence)
boundary: GPU core die only: top level (std cells, clock/repair buffers) + four quadrant hard blocks (mapped Vortex + command/memory adapters + OpenRAM macros); host, external DRAM and board power excluded
double_counting: blocks are measured from their own netlists and SPEF; at the top they are abstract liberty models checked to carry no internal/leakage power groups, so the top part counts only top-level cells and the switching of top-level nets (block pin capacitance as load)

replay_port_order.note:
Copy of the top netlist for the gate replay whose vector ports are declared in the bit order of the reference.

    The port trace is the MSB-first concatenation of the RTL ports, the replay maps it onto the netlist ports by
    position.  The partition's top declares the per-memory-port vectors [1:0] where the RTL (and the flat netlist,
    replay-equal to it) declares [0:1]: same bits by index (every connection names its bit), opposite MSB.  The copy
    differs from the netlist only in those declaration lines (asserted); the power uses the unchanged netlist's
    database and parasitics.

macro_power.note:
Copies of the OpenRAM macro libraries without internal_power groups.

    The OpenRAM analytical power model wrote access energies of 3e10..2e11 per
    edge (also in its own datasheets), i.e. no valid characterisation exists.
    Macro access energy is therefore excluded (reported with the per-macro
    access counts); macro leakage and pin capacitance (net switching) remain.

reason: Per-seed routed hierarchical netlist activity (top + 4 quadrant blocks) replayed with zero output mismatches; SPEF-based power of every part recorded
